task: Enable manual reindex for Git FAQ datasources from the list and details views, independent of scheduler state, without regressing other datasource types or the cron schedule.

key_reasoning.reason: Baseline is 2 components (dataSourceUtils.ts gating/dispatch, possibly DataSourceDetails.tsx) across the UI and business-logic layers, matching the clear 'one explicit branch per index type' convention already used by 8 sibling index types — but dataSourceUtils.ts is a shared utility consumed by every datasource type's reindex action, so a change here carries blast radius beyond Git FAQ, bumping Component Scope from M to L.

The branch-per-index-type pattern is well established (8 existing sibling implementations), so the baseline is S — but AC3 (actionable error on failure) and AC5 (no regression for other datasource types) are edge/variant cases, and technical-analysis.md's Testing Landscape/Risk Indicators confirm no test exists exercising canFullReindex/canForceReindex/performFullReindex for a Git FAQ item in an errored state. No existing test template covers this defensive scenario, so Technical Risk is bumped from S to M per the edge-case auto-bump rule.

The 5 acceptance criteria are concrete and the root cause is pinpointed, but technical-analysis.md itself flags two open design questions: whether DataSourceDetails.tsx needs an independent fix (it does not visibly route through dataSourceUtils.ts), and whether performFullReindex's new Git FAQ branch must mirror createOrUpdateGitFaqIndex's exact reindex payload shape (link/branch/files_filter/setting_id).

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from M to L: fix sits inside dataSourceUtils.ts, a core shared utility used by canFullReindex/canForceReindex/performFullReindex for every datasource type, not just Git FAQ.

Technical Risk bumped from S to M: acceptance criteria enumerate an error-path case (AC3) and a cross-type regression case (AC5) for which technical-analysis.md confirms no existing test currently exercises the Git FAQ + error:true scenario.
